items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 3:1
items.html: The head of Arich Anpin, the white hairs, and the hairs are each composed of three HaVaYaHs, namely the HaVaYaH of MA, which is direct light and the TZADIK of Tzelem; and the HaVaYaH of SAG and the HaVaYaH of AB, which are the two surrounding [lights] of the LAMED-MEM of Tzelem — the HaVaYaH of SAG being a small surrounding light and the HaVaYaH of AB being a great surrounding light. As above, Page 1000, Item 38; see there in Or Pnimi. And in these three HaVaYaHs there are twelve letters, and one that includes them all, namely the aspect of the screen and Malchut in them, upon which the coupling is made, which raises reflected light and clothes them. And it spreads from above downward and bestows these twelve to the lower ones; hence it is called the one that includes them all, for in this Malchut there are all twelve letters of these HaVaYaHs. Hence there are twelve white hairs — the twelve white paths seen between the hairs, which are the three above-mentioned HaVaYaHs — and one white path that includes them all, which is the aspect of Malchut in them, as above. Likewise there are twelve strands and a thirteenth strand that includes them all, and likewise twelve corrections of the beard and one that includes them all. For they are all included and divided according to the aspect of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem, which are twelve aspects, and one that includes them all, which is Malchut. And this path of the division of the hairs — namely the white line that divides between the hairs, from which the hairs separate to the right side and to the left side of the head — is that one white path that includes them all. (Page 356, Item 127; Item 175).
